description: Only transactions with an amount strictly greater than 2400 count, so an amount of exactly 2400 is excluded.

a.request: Considering only transactions whose amount (`trans.amount`) is greater than 2400, group them by operation (`trans.operation`), with transactions that have no operation forming their own group. For each group, show the operation; the average signed amount, where the amount counts as positive for credits (`trans.type` = 'PRIJEM'), as negative for withdrawals (`trans.type` = 'VYDAJ'), and is left out of the average for any other type; and the total number of transactions in the group, of any type.
a.sql: SELECT operation, AVG(CASE WHEN type = 'PRIJEM' THEN amount WHEN type = 'VYDAJ' THEN -amount END) AS avg_signed_amount, COUNT(*) AS total_transactions FROM trans WHERE amount > 2400 GROUP BY operation;

c.request: Treating 2400 as the cutoff for a large transaction amount (`trans.amount`), break the large transactions down by operation (`trans.operation`), with transactions that have no operation as their own group. For each group, show the operation; the average signed amount, positive for credits (`trans.type` = 'PRIJEM') and negative for withdrawals ('VYDAJ'), with any other type left out of the average; and how many large transactions the group has in total, of any type. Only transactions with an amount strictly greater than 2400 count, so an amount of exactly 2400 is excluded.
c.sql: SELECT operation, AVG(CASE WHEN type = 'PRIJEM' THEN amount WHEN type = 'VYDAJ' THEN -amount END) AS avg_signed_amount, COUNT(*) AS large_transaction_count FROM trans WHERE amount > 2400 GROUP BY operation;

b.request: Among trans rows with amount > 2400, group by operation (NULL operation as its own group): for each group, show the operation, AVG(CASE trans.type WHEN 'PRIJEM' THEN amount WHEN 'VYDAJ' THEN -amount END) ignoring other types, and COUNT of all large transactions regardless of type.
b.sql: SELECT operation, AVG(CASE type WHEN 'PRIJEM' THEN amount WHEN 'VYDAJ' THEN -amount END) AS avg_signed_amount, COUNT(*) AS large_transaction_count FROM trans WHERE amount > 2400 GROUP BY operation;
b.raw: Among trans rows with amount > 2400, group by operation (NULL operation as its own group): for each group, show the operation, AVG(CASE trans.type WHEN 'PRIJEM' THEN amount WHEN 'VYDAJ' THEN -amount END) ignoring other types, and COUNT of all large transactions regardless of type.

d.request: Group transactions with `trans.amount > 2400` by `trans.operation` (NULL operations as their own group), and for each group return the operation, the average of `amount` signed positive for `trans.type` = 'PRIJEM' and negative for 'VYDAJ' (other types excluded from the average), and the count of all large transactions in the group regardless of type.
d.sql: SELECT operation, AVG(CASE WHEN type = 'PRIJEM' THEN amount WHEN type = 'VYDAJ' THEN -amount END) AS avg_signed_amount, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM trans WHERE amount > 2400 GROUP BY operation;
